body:
Code changes: +397 -2\
Tests: +239 -0\
Others: +107 -2

## What

The new chat page's `/` menu now lists the agent's skills before the chat starts, including the first time you ever use that agent.

## Why

The page could only show skills that an earlier live session of the same agent had reported and cached. If that agent had never run a session (or never in this project), `/` showed nothing until after the first message. t3code avoids this by reading skills per provider and folder on the server, with no thread needed. This PR does the same.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| A new chat with an agent that has never run a session: `/` lists no skills | `/` lists the project's skills, the user's skills and the enabled Claude plugin skills, with no session needed |

On a dev host, `GET /api/v1/agents/claude-code/skills` returned 285 skills (57 from plugins, e.g. `compound-engineering:ce-plan`), and `GET /api/v1/agents/codex/skills` returned 258.

## How

- **`GET /api/v1/agents/{agent}/skills?projectId=`** (`service/chat/skill_scan.go`) reads the folders the agent itself loads skills from:
  - Claude Code: `<project>/.claude/skills` and `commands`, then the user's `skills` and `commands`, then each enabled plugin (from `installed_plugins.json` and `enabledPlugins` in user, project and local settings), namespaced by its manifest name. Project-scoped plugins only count in their own project. Skills marked `user-invocable: false` are skipped.
  - Codex: `<repo>/.agents/skills` and `.codex/skills`, `~/.agents/skills`, `~/.codex/skills`, and Codex's bundled `.system` skills.
  - The first entry of a name wins, project before user, as in the agents. Display names and short descriptions come from the existing `agents/openai.yaml` metadata.
  - `source` matches what the live drivers report (Claude `agent`, Codex scopes), so the badge stays the same when the chat starts.
- If a project doesn't resolve (Scratchpad, a removed project), the route still returns the user's own skills instead of an error. Other agents get an empty list.
- **New chat page:** `useAgentSkillsQuery` fetches the list for the selected agent, project and host. `mergeChatSkills` keeps any list a past session reported first and appends skills found on disk since then, so nothing reorders when the session takes over.
- A remote host on an older version returns 404 for this route. That 404 stays out of Sentry, and the page keeps its cached list.

Intentional omissions:
- Codex skills switched off in `config.toml` can still appear until a session starts and reports its real list.
- Agent built-ins like `/compact` appear only once a session of that agent has run, because no folder holds them.

## Testing

Local checks not run; GitHub Actions handles validation.

- New: `skill_scan_test.go` (ordering, enabled plugins only, manifest naming, project-only plugins, commands, hidden skills, Codex metadata, unknown agents), `agents_skills_test.go` (project, unknown project and no project through the router), and `useAgentSkillsQuery.test.ts` (merge order).
- Manual: called the route against a running dev daemon and opened `/` on the new chat page in the dev app.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [ ] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording (text before/after only, no screenshot)
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * The new-chat page now discovers skills and commands for supported agents, including Claude Code and Codex.
  * Claude Code skills can come from project and user folders, commands, and enabled plugins. Codex skills can come from repository, user, and system locations.
  * When available, project skills are listed before user skills. Discovered skills are combined with saved chat skills, keeping saved skills first and avoiding duplicate names.
  * Cloud tasks continue to use no skills.
